context.join: requirements[].name is the requirement name every claim in generated/requirements.json is judged against; the join is total in both directions
context.statements: statements[] are the design decisions and assumptions no numeric claim is judged against, including the choices that close the brief's open questions

requirements.name: above_VBOR8
requirements.rationale: the brief says 'above brown-out' without naming a number; the number that phrase refers to is the rising threshold of the option-byte level this board configures, which is a property of the chosen MCU rather than of the brief
requirements.statement: the logic rail stays above the MCU's brown-out reset threshold with every coil energising at once

requirements.name: above_must_operate
requirements.rationale: 'independently commandable' presupposes that a commanded coil actually transfers its contacts, which the relay states as a must-operate voltage
requirements.statement: the coil supply reaches the relay's must-operate voltage at the worst-case combination of input tolerance and series drops

alternatives_considered: no declared count, leaving the figure to be read off the board
requirements.name: as_declared
requirements.rationale: through-hole count drives the hand-soldering line on an assembly quote, so it is declared rather than discovered at quote time
requirements.statement: the number of through-hole parts matches the assembly policy this board declares

requirements.name: assumptions_agree_with_the_certification
requirements.rationale: the derivation picks a material group before any part is chosen; if the chosen barrier is certified for a worse group than the derivation assumed, the derived figure is optimistic
requirements.statement: the material group the clearance derivation assumed is no better than the one the barrier component is certified for

requirements.name: at_or_above_the_component_creepage
requirements.rationale: the relay body spans the boundary, so the board's own separation should not be the weaker of the two paths in parallel
requirements.statement: the boundary is at least as wide as the creepage the barrier component is itself certified for

requirements.name: at_or_above_the_planned_build_quantity
requirements.rationale: the relay is a single-sourced part with the lowest stock on the bill of materials, so the planned build quantity is a requirement on availability and not only on the design
requirements.statement: the catalogue can supply the planned build quantity of the binding part

requirements.name: at_or_above_the_reinforced_figure
requirements.rationale: the brief requires a figure 'derived from the documented rating'; the derivation is IEC 60664-1's creepage table at the selected pollution degree and material group, doubled for reinforced insulation
requirements.statement: the boundary is at least as wide as the reinforced creepage the documented rating requires

requirements.name: at_or_below_the_voh_test_current
requirements.rationale: the guaranteed drive level used by the gate claim is only guaranteed at the datasheet's stated test current; drawing more would make that level an extrapolation
requirements.statement: each command pin sources no more than the current its output-high level is specified at

alternatives_considered: a series Schottky, rejected because its drop would consume most of the margin between the input minimum and the coil's must-operate voltage
a larger drop absorbed by raising the input minimum, rejected because the brief fixes the input at 5 V
requirements.name: below_a_tenth_of_the_input
requirements.rationale: the brief requires reverse-polarity tolerance but says nothing about the forward drop it may cost; a tenth of the input is the budget this design allocates, and it is what leaves the coil rail above must-operate at the low end of the input tolerance
requirements.statement: the reverse-polarity device drops less than a tenth of the input voltage at full load

requirements.name: below_characterised_maximum
requirements.rationale: the brief's 'inside the MCU's operating range' is bounded above as well as below, and the upper bound is the datasheet's characterised supply maximum rather than its absolute maximum
requirements.statement: the logic rail stays inside the supply range the MCU is characterised over

requirements.name: below_coil_maximum
requirements.rationale: the same supply that must reach must-operate at its low end must not exceed the coil's continuous rating at its high end
requirements.statement: the coil supply stays below the relay's maximum continuous coil voltage

requirements.name: below_drain_source_breakdown
requirements.rationale: the brief requires clamping 'below the driver's breakdown voltage', which is the FET's BVdss plus the diode's forward drop as the clamp level
requirements.statement: the clamped turn-off voltage stays below the driver FET's drain-source breakdown

requirements.name: every_entering_conductor_clamped
requirements.statement: every logic-side conductor entering the board reaches a clamp, or is exempt for a stated reason

requirements.name: every_required_marking_present
requirements.statement: the silkscreen carries each terminal's channel and contact function and the per-channel maximum voltage and current

requirements.name: every_required_node_probed
requirements.statement: the 5 V rail, ground, the coil supply and every driver input and coil node reach a probe on the logic side

requirements.name: gate_at_or_above_characterised_drive
requirements.rationale: the brief asks for a stage 'fully on at the drive level the chosen MCU guarantees'; 'fully on' is only meaningful against a drive level the FET datasheet actually characterises
requirements.statement: each driver gate reaches at least the gate-source voltage the FET's on-resistance is characterised at

requirements.name: gate_below_threshold
requirements.rationale: the brief requires the input to be 'resistively held de-energised'; the level that qualifies as de-energised is the FET's own minimum threshold, not zero
requirements.statement: each driver gate stays below the FET's minimum gate-source threshold when the MCU pin does not drive it

requirements.name: no_copper_crosses_the_boundary
requirements.statement: no conductor lies inside the isolation boundary on any layer except the relay contact pins and their terminals

requirements.name: reinforced_clearance_at_category_III
requirements.rationale: the board is designed to category II; the relay carries a category III certification, and a boundary that fell short of category III would make the relay's certification the misleading part of the documentation
requirements.statement: the boundary also meets reinforced clearance at the overvoltage category the relay is certified for, not only the category this board is designed to

alternatives_considered: both sides populated, which would shrink the board but add a placement side to the assembly quote
logic parts on the back, rejected because it would put copper and parts on the layer the boundary keepout has to clear
requirements.name: single_placement_side
requirements.rationale: a single placement side halves assembly setup and removes the second-side reflow the through-hole parts would otherwise complicate; nothing on this board needs the second side
requirements.statement: every part is placed on the front side

requirements.name: switched_and_logic_copper_are_separated
requirements.statement: every conductor is wholly on the switched side or wholly on the logic side of the boundary

alternatives_considered: sizing against IPC-2152, which cannot be frozen into this repository as evidence
a wider conductor chosen without a stated rise, which would make the width unreviewable
requirements.name: temperature_rise_within_20C
requirements.rationale: the brief sets no conductor temperature limit; 20 degC is the rise this design sizes switched copper for. No conductor-sizing standard is frozen in this repository, so the rise at the marked current is not established here and the claim is reported as unknown rather than assumed to pass
requirements.statement: switched copper carries the marked current at no more than a 20 degC rise

requirements.name: within_absolute_maximum
requirements.rationale: an operating-range requirement does not by itself establish that the destructive limit is respected at the top of the input tolerance
requirements.statement: the supply pin never sees more than its absolute maximum rating

requirements.name: within_average_forward_current
requirements.rationale: the brief requires the flyback device to be 'rated for the coil current'; the applicable rating is the average forward current
requirements.statement: each flyback device carries the coil current within its average forward-current rating

requirements.name: within_forward_current
requirements.rationale: the brief requires status indication but sets no current; the ceiling is the LED's own rating
requirements.statement: each indicator runs below the LED's maximum forward current

requirements.name: within_gate_source_maximum
requirements.rationale: a gate-referenced reverse-polarity stage sees the full input across its gate-source junction when the input is reversed, which is the case the brief's 'tolerate reverse polarity' has to survive
requirements.statement: the reverse-polarity FET's gate-source stress stays within its maximum in either input polarity

requirements.name: within_ivcc_maximum
requirements.rationale: the rail model loads the MCU at a fixed current, and that figure has to be one the part is allowed to draw
requirements.statement: the MCU draws no more than the datasheet's maximum current into VCC

requirements.name: within_package_dissipation
requirements.rationale: the brief conditions this on maximum ambient; the package figures used here are the datasheet ratings at their own reference ambient, so this establishes the dissipation and not the junction temperature
requirements.statement: no part dissipates more than its package is rated for with all four channels on

requirements.name: within_per_pin_source_current
requirements.rationale: the brief's 'total pin current within ratings' is bounded per pin as well as in aggregate, and the per-pin figure is the tighter one here because each command pin also drives an indicator
requirements.statement: no MCU pin sources more than its per-pin absolute maximum

requirements.name: within_resistor_rating
requirements.rationale: the gate, pull-down and indicator networks were sized for current, and the dissipation that follows has to fit the 0603 body chosen
requirements.statement: every resistor dissipates less than its package rating

requirements.name: within_reverse_standoff
requirements.rationale: a clamp whose standoff is below the line's normal working voltage conducts in normal operation, so the brief's ESD requirement implies a standoff floor
requirements.statement: every clamp's reverse standoff voltage covers the working voltage of the conductor it protects

requirements.name: within_the_certified_insulation_voltage
requirements.rationale: the coil-to-contact barrier is the relay, and its certificate states the voltage that certification is valid at
requirements.statement: the documented switched voltage is within the rated insulation voltage the barrier component is certified at

requirements.name: within_the_component_rating
requirements.statement: the documented switched voltage and current are within the rating of every component in the switched path

alternatives_considered: no numeric target, with the loop left to the placement cost function, which cannot see loop area at all
a tighter target reached by placing the diode under the relay body, rejected because it puts copper where the coil pins need clearance
requirements.name: within_the_declared_loop_target
requirements.rationale: the brief asks for 'a small turn-off loop' without a number; a declared area target makes 'small' checkable and lets the placement search be told to leave the loop alone
requirements.statement: each flyback turn-off loop encloses no more than the declared area target

requirements.name: within_the_terminal_rating
requirements.rationale: the brief specifies a 5 V input but not what it may draw; the ceiling is set by the connector the input arrives through
requirements.statement: the total board input current stays within the input terminal's current rating

alternatives_considered: coils on the logic rail directly, rejected because four coils switching together would put the whole step across the MCU
a separate documented coil input, rejected because it would add a connector and a second supply the brief does not ask for
statements.name: coil_supply_topology
statements.rationale: the brief leaves this open; separating them keeps the coil turn-on step out of the MCU's supply, which is what makes the rail claim provable rather than marginal
statements.statement: the coils take their own rail downstream of the reverse-polarity device, and the logic rail is fed from it through a series element

alternatives_considered: an isolated host interface, rejected because the interface is already on the logic side of the reinforced barrier
local switch inputs, rejected because they would need their own debounce and ESD treatment for no requirement in the brief
statements.name: command_origin
statements.rationale: the brief leaves the origin and the isolation of the interface open; the interface is on the logic side of the boundary, so isolating it would add cost without changing what the boundary separates
statements.statement: channel commands originate in firmware on the on-board MCU, with a non-isolated UART header for a host

statements.invalidated_by: a measured source and harness resistance above the budget, which would lower the coil rail and could put it below must-operate
statements.name: input_path_budget
statements.reason: the brief specifies an external 5 V input but nothing about the impedance behind it, and every rail claim depends on it
statements.statement: the field wiring and the source feeding the input terminal together present no more than 0.5 ohm

statements.invalidated_by: an installation at pollution degree 3, which the relay is certified for but which the frozen table subset in this repository carries no column for
statements.name: installation_environment
statements.reason: the brief does not describe the installation, and the creepage and clearance figures cannot be derived without it
statements.statement: the board is installed in a pollution degree 2, material group III, overvoltage category II environment

statements.invalidated_by: any stated maximum ambient above the package ratings' reference ambient, which would derate every package figure these claims are judged against
statements.name: maximum_ambient
statements.reason: the brief conditions the dissipation requirement on 'maximum ambient' without stating one, and this board does not yet state one either; the dissipation figures are therefore established but the junction temperatures they imply are not
statements.statement: the maximum ambient the dissipation claims are evaluated at is the reference ambient of the package ratings they are compared against

alternatives_considered: a larger STM32, rejected as unnecessary I/O and cost for four channels
a part with a defined pull-up at reset, rejected because it would fight the gate pull-downs during reset
statements.name: mcu_selection
statements.rationale: the brief leaves the MCU open subject to I/O count, a defined reset state and adequate guaranteed drive; this part has all three, is stocked in the assembly catalogue, and its floating-input reset state is what lets the coils be held off by the pull-downs alone
statements.statement: channel commands come from a PY32F003F18P6TU in a TSSOP-20 package

alternatives_considered: Omron G5Q-14 DC5, which would cut the bill of materials by 39 percent and quadruple available stock, rejected because its normally-closed contact is rated 3 A rather than 16 A and its certified creepage is 6.4 mm rather than 8 mm
statements.name: relay_selection
statements.rationale: it is a current product with a VDE reinforced coil-to-contact certification at 250 V, 8 mm of certified creepage and a 16 A contact rating, which leaves the board's 4 A rating limited by parts that are cheap to change
statements.statement: the barrier component is the Omron G2RL-1-E DC5

alternatives_considered: the relay's full 16 A, rejected because the terminals and the switched copper would have to grow to carry it
a low-voltage DC-only rating, rejected because it would waste the reinforced barrier the relay already provides
statements.name: switched_rating
statements.rationale: the brief makes the rating the designer's choice and derives the clearances from it; 4 A is well inside the relay's 16 A contact rating and is set by the terminal and the switched copper rather than by the relay
statements.statement: the documented switched rating is 250 V rms at 4 A per channel

alternatives_considered: normally-closed, common, normally-open, which has no planar solution for this relay's contact pin order
statements.name: terminal_function_order
statements.rationale: the three contact paths have to reach the terminal without crossing and without a via, because no switched conductor may leave the front layer; that constraint has exactly one planar solution, and this is it
statements.statement: each switched terminal presents its contacts in the order normally-open, common, normally-closed
